output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise is not mainly a handling problem. Since 1 Sep, Corvane's bag tags at Harlow Bay have been printed on new Fennick stock. Those tags fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% before. Bags that can't be read go to the manual encode desk, where the evening wait rose from 7 to about 30 minutes. 91% of the bags lost on that path reached the lateral after it had closed. Bags on the automatic path are unchanged. Pelion, which uses the same Tessaly crews, is flat. In 14–16 Oct, counters using old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6% while kiosks on Fennick stock failed at 12%. So the new stock, or how the printers are set up for it, is the cause. The evidence can't yet say whether the stock itself is defective or the printer heat setting is wrong, so hold off on a defect claim against Fennick. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock held in stores (valid contract to 31 Dec), then check the rate over a couple of weeks. Test Fennick stock separately with the printer settings corrected. Optionally ask the airport authority for an extra encode workstation in the evening as a stopgap. I'm fairly confident in this; the main open question is whether the stock or the settings are at fault.
